data.name: Kamesh
data.long_meaning: Kamesh is the Hindu god of wealth, prosperity, and desire. He is depicted as having four hands, each holding a symbol of abundance: a bowl of gold coins, a lotus, a rosary, and a goad.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the desire for spiritual growth and abundance in all aspects of life.

vedic_reference.note: Kamesh is a variant name for Kamadeva, the god of love in Hinduism. Kamadeva is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures, including the Rigveda and the Mahabharata.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kamesh evokes a feeling of richness and abundance, both materially and spiritually. It is a name often invoked in Hinduism for happiness, success, and wealth. The choices one makes by associating with this name can influence their own personal realm of richness and prosperity, leading to a more exuberant and fulfilled life.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeper level, the name Kamesh holds spiritual meaning, reminding us of the universal desire for happiness and contentment. It is a reminder to focus on inner wealth and prosperity, as well as material riches. The name Kamesh brings us back to the Unchanging, Blissful Reality, beyond the ever-changing play of the material world.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Kamesh is a name mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic. The name Kamesh carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Kamesh is a god in Hinduism, often depicted as the god of love and desire.

modern_usage.modern_context: In modern usage, Kamesh is a common name for boys in the Indian subcontinent and among people of Indian origin living abroad. It is also a popular name on social media platforms and in online gaming communities.

name_in_real_life.story: Radha Kamesh, a teacher in Kathmandu, Nepal, shares that their name Kamesh meaning "God of Wealth" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Kamesh, the embodiment of desire and pleasure, symbolizes the human longing for sensory experiences and material wealth. It is a reminder that life is an expression of our deepest desires and passions.
